text: The pivotal sentence in Genesis 6 concerns God's inner life: Yahweh sees that "every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually," is sorry that he made man, and is "grieved in his heart" (Genesis 6:5-6). That grief comes before the sentence of judgment, and it gives the judgment its character. The flood is moved by a maker's sorrow over what his creatures have become. Before any rain falls, however, the first covenant in Scripture appears: "I will establish my covenant with you," God tells Noah, "and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you" (Genesis 6:18). The promise reaches beyond Noah to the animals, two of every sort, and to the food that will keep them all alive (Genesis 6:19-21). Genesis 6 announces "the end of all flesh" and also arranges, in detail, what will survive it. Noah, the one man who found favor with God, is told to gather in the creatures God is about to drown.
